intro: Learn how to express strong preferences with encantar, specify who enjoys something, and agree or disagree.
b1.texto:
With verbs like **gustar** and **encantar**, the liked thing is the subject and the verb agrees with it:

- Me **gusta** bailar / Me **encanta** cocinar. (activities in infinitive: singular verb)
- Me **encantan** los libros. (plural noun: plural verb)

To show who likes something, use indirect object pronouns: **me, te, le, nos, os, les**.
If you name the person, precede with **a** and keep the pronoun: **A Pablo le** encanta el fútbol.

To agree:
- Positive statement: *Me gusta el cine.* → **A mí también.** (disagree: **A mí no.**)
- Negative statement: *No me gusta bailar.* → **A mí tampoco.** (disagree: **A mí sí.**)
b4.texto: Notice that infinitives keep the verb in singular, whereas plural nouns require a plural verb.
b6.pregunta: «No me gusta el café». Neither do you. What do you reply?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Exactly! Tampoco is used to agree with a negative statement.
b6.o1.refuerzo: También is only used after positive statements.
b6.o2.refuerzo: A mí sí indicates disagreement (you do like it).
b7.pregunta: Choose the correct form of the verb.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct! Infinitives require the singular verb form.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Gustan is used with plural nouns.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Gusto is not the right grammatical form here.
p.me encanta.consejo: Used for strong liking of an activity or singular item.
p.me encantan.consejo: Plural form agreeing with plural items.
p.le gusta.consejo: Used for he, she, or formal you.
p.le encanta.consejo: He or she loves something intensely.
p.les gusta.consejo: Used for they or plural you.
p.el fútbol.consejo: Masculine noun with an accent on the u.
p.la música.consejo: Feminine noun with an accent on the u.
p.a mí también.consejo: To agree with an affirmative statement.
p.a mí tampoco.consejo: To agree with a negative statement.
p.a mí sí.consejo: To disagree with a previous negative statement.
p.a mí no.consejo: To disagree with a previous positive statement.
p.nada.consejo: Reinforces negation: no me gusta nada.
b2.f0.texto: What do you like doing on Sundays?
b4.e0.texto: We like dancing and cooking at home.
b5.f0.texto: On our days off we like cooking together in the kitchen.
b5.f1.texto: Lucía loves preparing dishes with rice and fresh vegetables.
b5.f2.texto: My brother Pablo doesn't like cooking at all at weekends.
b5.f3.texto: In the afternoons my parents love listening to classical music.
b5.f4.texto: All of us really like books about ancient history.
b5.f5.texto: I don't like wasting time doing nothing interesting either.
b8.frase: A mi hermano le encanta el fútbol.
p.encantan.consejo: Works like «gustar»: plural thing, plural verb. «Me encantan los libros» = I love books.
p.libres.consejo: One form for masculine and feminine: «libre». «Días libres» are days off.
p.arroz.consejo: The rr sound starts the stressed syllable: a-RROTH. The z becomes c in the plural: «arroces».
p.frescas.consejo: Feminine plural of «fresco», agreeing with «verduras». The c before a sounds like k.
p.encanta.consejo: It stays singular before a verb: «le encanta preparar», «le encanta cocinar».
p.clásica.consejo: The stress falls on the first syllable, so it has an accent: KLA-si-ka. «Música clásica».
p.interesante.consejo: One form for masculine and feminine: «interesante». The stress is on «san»: in-te-re-SAN-te.
